home.heading: Look after your stream, protect your neighbours
home.intro: Urban streams can host mosquitoes that carry West Nile virus. Frogs, birds and bats eat them. Your 15-minute check tells the city where water is standing still and predators are missing.
home.promise1: AI only suggests. You decide every answer.
home.promise2: Nothing happens automatically. A city officer approves every action.
home.promise3: We describe habitat, never disease. We never diagnose people, birds or places.
home.promise4: You stay anonymous. We store a random code, never your name or email.
home.sourceNote: Based on the OneAquaHealth Policy Brief (2026) and field protocols.

common.photoAdded: Photo added. Location data removed and size reduced.
common.photoError: That file could not be read as a photo.

site.heading: Which stream are you at?
site.intro: Choose one of the OneAquaHealth research sites. Your exact position is never stored, only a point rounded to about 100 m.
site.locationDenied: Location is off. Choose a site from the list instead.
site.loadError: Sites could not be loaded. Check your connection and try again.

stream.heading: Stream check
stream.intro: Look along about 50 m of the stream. Answer what you can see from the bank. Do not step into the water.
stream.source: Questions from the OneAquaHealth field form (Annex I).
stream.scaleHelp: Present means you can see it. Extensive means it covers more than a third of the channel.

sections.channel_substrate: What the stream bed is made of
sections.banks: What the banks are made of

q.flow_NP: Still water (no flow you can see)
q.flow_D: Dry patches or flow that stops
q.barriers: Weirs or dams across the stream
q.mac_broad_leaved_herbs: Tall broad-leaved plants growing out of the water

larvae.heading: Larval dip
larvae.intro: Mosquito larvae live in still, shallow water at the edges. Five quick dips with a cup show whether they are breeding here.
larvae.why: Standing water at the stream edge is where Culex mosquitoes, the main West Nile virus vectors in Europe, lay their eggs.
larvae.how1: Find still water at the edge, among plants if possible. Stay on the bank.
larvae.how2: Lower a white cup at an angle so water flows in gently. Do not splash.
larvae.how3: Wait 10 seconds, then count the small wriggling larvae.
larvae.how4: Pour the water back. Repeat at five different spots.
larvae.safety: Wash your hands afterwards. Never drink stream water.
larvae.postureQuestion: How do most larvae rest at the surface?
larvae.postureHelp: Look at the cup from the side for a few seconds.
larvae.posture_angled: Hanging at an angle, head down
larvae.posture_flat: Lying flat, parallel to the surface
larvae.keyCulex: Guided key: hanging at an angle with a breathing tube suggests a Culex-type or Aedes-type larva.
larvae.keyAnopheles: Guided key: lying flat suggests an Anopheles-type larva.
larvae.keyNote: This is a type, never a species, and says nothing about disease.
larvae.noLarvae: No larvae in any dip. That is useful data too.

predators.heading: Mosquito predators
predators.intro: Frogs, toads, insect-eating birds and bats keep mosquito numbers down. Where they are missing, mosquitoes do better.
predators.why: The OneAquaHealth Policy Brief reports fewer insect predators at degraded streams, weakening natural mosquito control.
predators.photo: Photo of an animal (optional, from a distance)

deadBirds.heading: Dead birds
deadBirds.warning1: Do not touch, move or pick up the bird, even with gloves.
deadBirds.warning3: Take a photo only from where you stand.
deadBirds.why: Clusters of dead birds can be an early sign that the city's veterinary team should look. We report and route. We never diagnose.
deadBirds.question: Did you see any dead birds?
deadBirds.routing: Your report goes to the city's veterinary team for follow-up.

review.heading: Check and send
review.consent: I agree that my anonymous answers and photos can be used by the city and the OneAquaHealth research team.
review.consentRequired: Please tick the box to send.

done.heading: Thank you!
done.queued: Your check-in is saved on this device and will be sent when you are online.
done.next: We will tell you if it helps raise an alert or leads to an action.

ai.thinking: Asking the AI for a suggestion...
ai.chipLabel: AI suggestion, waiting for your decision
ai.mustDecide: You decide. Unanswered suggestions are not sent.
ai.unavailable: AI unavailable, answer manually. Your photo is still saved with the check-in.
ai.droppedTitle: The AI also gave an answer that is not on our allowed list, so we removed it:
ai.implausible: GBIF has {{n}} records of this species near here. An expert will review this record.
ai.disagree: The key says “{{key}}” but the AI suggests “{{ai}}”. Look again and choose what fits best.

adult.heading: Adult mosquitoes (optional)
adult.intro: Did a mosquito land on you or can you see one resting nearby? Answer the key first. Only an expert can confirm a species.
adult.question: Did you see an adult mosquito?
adult.q_stripes: Does it have black and white stripes on the legs and body?
adult.q_thorax_line: Is there one white line down the middle of its back?
adult.q_colour: Is it plain brown or light brown?
adult.tigerNote: Tiger mosquitoes can spread dengue and chikungunya. Your report helps the city check.
adult.result_striped_aedes_type: Tiger mosquito type (Aedes albopictus-like). Only an expert can confirm the species.

calib.heading: Practice round
calib.intro: Answer {{n}} quick questions about drawings of streams and larvae. We compare your answers with the reference answers and show where your eye differs. It takes about five minutes.
calib.why: Everyone sees streams a little differently. Knowing how you tend to answer lets the city weigh each report fairly. Your tier never limits what you can report.
calib.referenceNote: The drawings are generated from their answers, so the answer is fixed by construction. No AI labelled them. They are synthetic and await review by the team panel.
calib.q_larval_posture: How do the larvae in this cup rest at the surface?
calib.kappaHelp: 1 means you matched every reference answer. 0 means no better than chance.
calib.tierHelp: Calibrated from 0.4 and Trusted from 0.7. Tiers set how much weight your answers get when several people check the same site.
calib.question: Question
calib.feedbackHeading: What to look for next time
calib.noFeedback: You matched every reference answer. Great eye!
calib.answeredVs: You answered {{ans}}; the reference answer is {{ref}}.
calib.savedOffline: You are offline, so your tier is saved on this device only for now.

bank_CC.under: You tend to rate banks as natural when hard revetment is visible. Look for straight edges and block joints, even under moss.
bank_CC.over: You rated some natural banks as concrete. Stones in a wire mesh (gabions) and soil are not concrete.

flow_NP.under: You tend to miss still water. Look for flat, dark water, floating leaves and reflections at the edges.
flow_NP.over: You tend to see still water where it is moving. White standing waves and ripples mean the water flows.

rip_trees.under: You tend to underestimate tree cover along the banks.
rip_trees.over: You tend to overestimate tree cover along the banks.

water_foam.under: You tend to miss foam on the water. Look for white patches that do not move with the ripples.
water_foam.over: You tend to report more foam than there is. A few small patches count as present, not extensive.

larval_posture.swap: Check the angle from the side: Culex-type larvae hang down from the surface, Anopheles-type larvae lie flat along it.

city.heading: City view
city.intro: Vector-habitat risk at each research site, from weather and volunteer stream checks. It describes conditions that favour mosquitoes, never infection.
city.seasonHelp: Weather is the same for every site. It scales the index; volunteer evidence decides which sites stand out.
city.mapLabel: Map of sites coloured by risk band. The table below has the same information.
city.noScores: No risk scores yet for this city.
city.trendLabel: Line chart of the weekly risk index for {{name}} with its range and the alert threshold at {{threshold}}.
city.trendTable: Show the trend as a table
city.queueIntro: The system drafts actions. Nothing is sent until an officer approves.
city.officerHelp: Recorded with your decision. Required to approve or dismiss.
city.notCatalogue: Operational step, not a Catalogue measure
city.officerRequired: Enter your officer name or code first.
